newsitem.title: USA: Gibson to speed up new products placement.
newsitem.headline: Gibson to speed up new products placement.

text.p: Gibson Greetings Inc reporting lower operating income for the second quarter, said Wednesday it plans to speed up new products placements at its retail outlets.
The company reported a net income of $5.4 million, or $0.32 per share, in the quarter ended June 30, compared to a $5.9 million net, or $0.36 per share, last year.
A First Call poll of four analysts had put the company's earnings at $0.35 a share for the quarter.
Gibson said the 1997 quarter included a $1.1 million charge, while the 1997 quarter included a $2.5 million gain, partly offset by a $0.5 million charge.

All the same, Gibson's quarterly operating income declined to $10.1 million, from 11.4 million last year. The company attributed the decline to cutting staff and increased marketing costs, which were partially offset by lower product costs and bad debt expense.

Gibson's quarterly revenues rose 4.6 percent to $92.7 million from 88.6 million last year. The company ascribed the rise to improved returns at its Gibson's Card Division; continued growth at its U.S. chain of 190 retail stores (Paper Factory of Wisconsin Inc); and higher sales at its Gibson Greetings International Ltd unit.

Chief executive Frank O'Connell said in a statement Gibson is implementing its strategy to become an entertainment company. The company recently has launched greeting-card type products such as three-dimensional cards and gift wraps with movie themes, a Gibson spokeswoman added.

"In the last six months we have created more than 5,000 new products across a variety of product categories, O'Connell said. "Our plans call for us to accelerate placement of these new products at retail."

O'Connell added Gibson is "financially poised to pursue an acquisition strategy" with a healthy cash balance and very little debt. He said the company will pursue the sale of the Paper Factory retail stores chain.
The company's stock rose 9/16 to 20-1/2 Wednesday.
